sources.author: Browne, Ed
sources.title: DARPA Denies Funding Wuhan Institute of Virology Amid Alleged Document Leak
sources.summary: Newsweek report that DARPA denied funding the EcoHealth DEFUSE proposal involving WIV after DRASTIC leaked the document—proposal rejected, not awarded.
sources.book_role: Clarifies DEFUSE was rejected by DARPA while situating it inside the U.S. biodefense funding machine Chapter 15 maps.

sources.author: Robinson, Nathan
sources.title: Why the Chair of the Lancet’s COVID-19 Commission Thinks The US Government Is Preventing a Real Investigation Into the Pandemic
sources.summary: Current Affairs interview with Jeffrey Sachs arguing he is ‘pretty convinced’ COVID came from U.S. lab biotechnology and that Washington blocks a real origins investigation amid dangerous unregulated virus research.
sources.book_role: Prominent commission chair pointing the biodefense finger back at U.S. labs and secrecy.

sources.author: Rindsberg, Ashley
sources.title: How Dick Cheney created Anthony Fauci
sources.summary: UnHerd essay arguing post-9/11 Cheney-era biodefense strategy elevated Fauci’s role and built the risky pathogen-research complex that later backfired.
sources.book_role: Historical thesis for Chapter 15: U.S. biodefense politics created the institutional world of GoF and pandemic preparedness.

sources.author: Richards, Stephanie, et al.
sources.title: BSL-3 Laboratory Practices in the United States: Comparison of Select Agent and Non–Select Agent Facilities
sources.publication: Biosecurity and Bioterrorism: Biodefense Strategy, Practice, and Science
sources.summary: 2014 survey comparing BSL-3 practices at U.S. select-agent versus non–select-agent facilities—empirical look at biosafety variation inside the domestic biodefense lab network.
sources.book_role: Technical evidence that U.S. high-containment practice itself is uneven—context for exporting risky work abroad.

sources.author: Baric, Ralph
sources.title: Synthetic Viral Genomics: Risks and Benefits for Science and Society
sources.summary: 2007 Baric paper on risks and benefits of synthetic viral genomics—early articulation of dual-use coronavirus reverse-genetics capabilities from a central U.S. practitioner.
sources.book_role: Primary statement from Baric on synthetic virus tech’s dual-use stakes inside the biodefense complex.

sources.author: Xu, Dezhong, et al.
sources.title: The Unnatural Origin of SARS and New Species of Artificial Humanized Viruses as Genetic Weapons
sources.publication: Academy of Military Medical Sciences Press
sources.summary: 2015 Chinese Academy of Military Medical Sciences Press book on unnatural SARS origin and artificial humanized viruses as genetic weapons. No URL in source data.
sources.book_role: Chinese military-medical literature treating humanized viruses as genetic weapons—mirror image of U.S. biodefense dual-use discourse.

orgs: Academy of Military Medical Sciences Press

sources.title: Anthrax scientist commits suicide as FBI closes in
sources.summary: AP/CBC report on Bruce Ivins’s suicide as FBI prepared to indict him in the 2001 anthrax-letter attacks—foundational trauma of the U.S. biodefense era.
sources.book_role: Historical anchor: domestic bioweapons lab insider threat that turbocharged post-anthrax biodefense spending.
